papers.title: Tetrodotoxin-resistant NaV1.8 contributes to action potential conduction in a population of mouse and human vagal nerve fibers
papers.abstract: Axonal action potential (AP) conduction is dependent on voltage-gated sodium channels (NaV1s). AP conduction in the vagus nerve (which contains afferent and efferent fibers) is essential to its reflex regulation of most visceral organs. The nine isoforms of NaV1s show diverse expression patterns in vagal neurons. In rodent vagus nerves, multiple NaV1 isoforms contribute to AP conduction, with NaV1.7 playing an essential role in ~70% of fibers. Here, we investigated the contribution of tetrodotoxin-resistant (TTX-R) NaV1.8 towards vagal AP conduction ex vivo. We tested two structurally different NaV1.8-selective inhibitors, A803467 and PF01247324 and their effects on electrically evoked C-fiber compound action potentials (CAPs) along mouse and human vagus nerves. Tetrodotoxin completely abolished mouse and human vagal CAPs. Nevertheless, both A803467 and PF01247324 caused a concentration-dependent decrease in the C-fiber CAPs in mouse and human vagus nerves. The selectivity of both drugs was tested in NaV1.8 knockout mice. A803467 but not PF01247324 significantly decreased NaV1.8 KO vagal CAPs, indicating that PF01247324's inhibition of wildtype vagal CAPs was solely mediated by NaV1.8, and that A803467 caused inhibition via NaV1.8-mediated and non-NaV1.8-mediated mechanisms. In further studies of wildtype mice, NaV1.8 inhibition following incubation with NaV1.7-selective inhibitor PF05089771 showed no further decrease in mouse vagal CAP, demonstrating that NaV1.8-dependent inhibition affects fibers also sensitive to NaV1.7-dependent inhibition. These data suggest that TTX-sensitive NaV1.7 and TTX-R NaV1.8 cooperate to conduct APs along a select population of vagal nerves. Axonal NaV1.8 inhibition could be utilized to treat aberrant vagal nerve activity in visceral organ diseases.

papers.title: Velocity-dependent friction in a simple two-oscillator system. I. Phase amplitude coupling
papers.abstract: Cortical gamma oscillations often arrive in bursts locked to the phase of slower theta waves, a pattern called theta gamma phase amplitude coupling (PAC). PAC is linked to memory and altered in epilepsy, but most models tie it to particular cells or circuits. We start from a generalized Langevin equation, an equation of motion for a few collective variables in which friction and random forces stand for the unobserved neural activity, and let its stiffness and friction depend on the state. Expanding them to first order in the theta and gamma variables yields ten possible interaction terms; only the two friction type terms change gamma energy and produce PAC, and depending on the term and its sign the gamma bursts sit at the peak, trough, rising or falling phase of theta. We study a gamma friction that follows theta velocity as a simplified example. Because the time integral of theta velocity is theta coordinate, the gamma amplitude rises and falls with theta coordinate as exp(gvvx{theta}/2). The fluctuation dissipation theorem turns noise and damping into a theta effective temperature, and the PAC strength becomes a closed form function of one dimensionless number, kappa , that combines the coupling with this temperature. Without fitted parameters, this prediction accounts for 51,095 simulated records (R2 = 0.993) and for the median PAC of 5,160 combinations of coupling and damping (R2 = 0.989). The coupling also drives gamma out of equilibrium: its kinetic temperature grows far above the one inferred from its response. All coefficients enter linearly so that they can, in principle, be estimated from recordings by linear regression. A companion paper shows that the same number sets the distance to a stability boundary.

papers.title: Velocity-dependent friction in a simple two-oscillator system. II. Regions of stability
papers.abstract: In Part I, a gamma friction that follows theta velocity produced theta gamma phase amplitude coupling (PAC) whose strength is a closed-form function of one dimensionless number, kappa;. Here we ask when this coupling destabilizes the gamma oscillator. The friction on gamma is negative during part of every theta cycle, yet gamma stays bounded: as long as it keeps oscillating, the energy gained while theta rises is returned while theta falls, and Liouville' sformula fixes the growth over a theta cycle at the baseline decay, whatever the coupling. Instability arises only in rare large theta cycles in which the friction exceeds critical damping, so that gamma stops oscillating and the gain is no longer returned. The typical trajectory becomes unstable when such cycles, about one in a hundred, outweigh the decay in all the others. This gives a boundary g* {sigma}x = 10, where {sigma}x is the typical theta amplitude set by the fluctuation dissipation theorem; the prediction agrees with a direct Lyapunov scan to within 6% for damping ratios from 0.0005 to 0.0055. The distance to the boundary is set by the same number kappa that sets the PAC strength, so that stronger PAC means closer proximity to instability. The mean-square boundary lies far lower but is set by events of negligible probability. Stimulating theta at or below its own frequency raises gamma energy and PAC and can drive giant gamma bursts or divergence, but no self-sustained activity, suggesting that a transition to seizure requires memory.

papers.title: Early Life Shift in Fear Extinction is Driven by Prefrontal-Amygdala Engagement
papers.abstract: The medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) displays a delayed maturation long hypothesized to guide developmental changes in threat processing. Nevertheless, the mechanism by which ontogenetic changes in mPFC function guide the developmental emergence of behavior is unclear. Early life marks a shift between a permanent extinction phenotype typical of juveniles, toward the standard, more transient extinction seen in adult rodents. This shift coincides with developmental changes in mPFC-amygdala connectivity, a pathway necessary for extinction processing in adults. Here we used optogenetics and slice electrophysiology to show that, in contrast to adult animals, juvenile mice displaying permanent extinction fail to engage the mPFC-amygdala pathway at the synaptic, cell activity or behavioral levels. Consistent with a requirement of this pathway for the developmental transition in extinction types, optic potentiation of the mPFC-amygdala pathway accelerates the onset of adult extinction. Our findings show that the developmental onboarding of the mPFC-amygdala pathway drives a shift in extinction processing toward increased fear reemergence that persists throughout adulthood.

papers.title: Harmonizing resting-state functional MRI data to increase sample size and to classify tinnitus brain connectivity
papers.abstract: Tinnitus, or ringing in the ears, is a hearing disorder that affects approximately 15% of human adults globally. The neuroscientific understanding of this subjective disorder is limited at present, partly due to a lack of sufficient neuroimaging data to compensate for the heterogeneity in the disorder; neural data acquisition is often impeded by low patient counts and doubled costs against scanning ample controls. However, with the increase in data sharing practices, data scarcity can be overcome with harmonization methods if scans from independent sites and studies are pooled successfully. To achieve data harmonization for limited data from a tinnitus neuroimaging study, we merged a modest fMRI dataset acquired in our lab (n=35) with age- and gender-matched samples from another large dataset, the Lifespan Human Connectome Project Aging (n=377). We measured functional connectivity (FC) between brain regions based on resting-state fMRI session scans, and used deep learning architecture to systematically combine individual FCs across the datasets. We assembled and trained neural network modules to purge dataset-identifying information from FC maps, and retained patterns that can characterize tinnitus-related FC. Hallmark artifactual information of the datasets was significantly reduced while reconstructing resting state FC data. Relevant relationships in brain connectivity that discern the condition of tinnitus from controls were well-preserved in the reconstructed resting state FC data. In agreement with existing literature on brain networks of tinnitus, connectivity related to default mode, ventral attention and frontoparietal control networks were identified to be crucial for distinguishing the condition, as masking these networks connections severely impacted downstream classification prediction on reconstructed FC. The data harmonization model was successful in merging FC matrices from independently acquired fMRI datasets, without losing out on meaningful functional connectivity patterns of interest for the neuropsychological disorder of tinnitus. Our findings demonstrate the potential of data harmonization by integrating independently acquired datasets on healthy controls to overcome neuroimaging data scarcity while preserving disorder-relevant neural signatures, advancing research on understudied neurological disorders.

papers.title: BrainRoute integrates machine learning prediction with community-driven verification of blood-brain barrier permeability
papers.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) is a highly selective barrier that restricts the entry of many therapeutic agents into the brain. The lack of efficient methods for BBB permeability research and data management remains a significant challenge for central nervous system drug-development pipelines. Although BBB permeability data are available from multiple open sources, few platforms integrate these datasets with molecular exploration, predictive tools, and a structured process for community-supported data verification. Here, we present BrainRoute, an open platform for BBB molecular data collection, exploration, prediction, and community-supported verification. BrainRoute provides searchable and filterable molecular records, physicochemical and structural information, source-linked data, single-molecule and batch prediction, and a structured workflow through which users can submit additional evidence for review. The prediction tool model-development cohort contained 7,888 unique molecules, including 5,424 BBB+ and 2,464 BBB- molecules. Six machine-learning classifiers were evaluated using PaDEL descriptors, Morgan fingerprints, frozen ChemBERTa embeddings, and combined feature representations. The three selected models were integrated into the platform as a probability-averaged ensemble. The primary five-fold scaffold-grouped analysis achieved a best mean balanced accuracy of 0.783 {+/-} 0.026. On an independent external set containing 410 non-overlapping molecules, the deployed ensemble achieved a balanced accuracy of 0.659 (95% CI 0.600 - 0.712) and an AUPRC of 0.670 (95% CI 0.583 - 0.752). BrainRoute serves as a platform for exploring BBB-related molecular data and computational predictions while supporting the continued growth and verification of the underlying dataset. BrainRoute is freely accessible online (https://github.com/omicscodeathon/brainroutedb).

papers.title: When spike sorting matters: single-neuron identity in the quantification of neural circuits
papers.abstract: Multiunit threshold crossings support high-performance brain-computer interfaces and preserve the low-dimensional trajectories that summarize population dynamics, raising the question of when spike sorting is still necessary. Using previously published recordings from four rhesus monkeys, we analyzed areas 3b and 1 of primary somatosensory cortex and ventral premotor cortex during a bimodal detection task, and ventral premotor cortex during an interval comparison task. From the same spikes, we built three representations: putative single units obtained with nonlinear sorting (UMAP and HDBSCAN), intermingled units obtained with linear sorting, and unsorted multiunit activity. Nonlinear sorting resolved up to three times more units than multiunit activity. In area 1, mixing discarded the periodicity information carried by phase-locked neurons, lengthened intrinsic timescales by about 40%, increased trial-to-trial variability, and raised neurometric detection thresholds by 33%. In premotor cortex, mixing reduced the task-related information recovered from the population and hid significant dimensions of its dynamics. After geometric alignment, the overall shape of population trajectories was nearly identical across representations, but distances between population states were distorted, and the approximately linear representation of interval duration saturated for longer intervals. Multiunit activity is therefore sufficient for analyses that rely on the dominant, shared structure of population activity, such as decoding, whereas analyses of single-neuron coding, variability, timescales, dimensionality, and parametric representations often require spike sorting.

papers.title: PolyMorph3D: A flexible MATLAB-based tool for quantifying microglia morphology and multi-colocalization in three dimensions
papers.abstract: As the principle immune cell of the central nervous system (CNS), microglia have been extensively studied throughout development and in a wide range of disease states. Of special focus have been their morphological features such as branching complexity, physical cell-cell interactions with surroundings, and gene expression readouts relating to phagocytosis and cytokine signaling. Each of these domains offers a window onto microglia function, and high-resolution confocal microscopy has long been a workhorse technique to visualize all three. A comprehensive view of microglia function requires both high-fidelity quantification with 3D resolution and colocalization of microglia with functional proteins such as those related to phagocytosis and with nearby structures such as synapses. Accordingly, a number of analytical tools have been developed to measure these features. However, existing open-source options lack either colocalization or 3D capability, while commercial solutions can be costly. Here, we sought to develop an open-source solution that addresses each of these limitations. PolyMorph3D is a MATLAB-based program capable of yielding individual cell-level data of microglia morphology and overlap with up to 4 other sources, all in 3D. The pipeline can be used effectively in mouse tissue and in human postmortem brain, thereby offering a flexible, low cost, and high-fidelity solution for the analysis of microglial morphology and function.

papers.title: Trial history and model-derived reward prediction errors in mousevisual decisions
papers.abstract: A reward prediction error (RPE) estimated from an animal's behavior can predict its next choice. Part of this predictive value may come from information about earlier trials that a choice model could also use directly. We asked whether a model-derived RPE improves choice prediction beyond the observable history of stimuli, choices, and rewards. We analyzed 275,292 trials from 107 mice performing the International Brain Laboratory visual decision task and evaluated the main choice models on sessions that were not used for fitting. Recent choices strongly improved prediction. An RPE based on a stimulus-dependent reward expectation added a small gain beyond the preceding choice and reward, and this gain fell to near zero once the model included the preceding stimulus. When the model also summarized choices and rewards over several earlier trials, an RPE trace with the same retention parameter as the history traces did not reliably improve prediction. In simulated agents with known decision rules, a simplified version of this comparison detected an RPE-based learning rule in which choices depended on accumulated prediction errors, and did not improve prediction for an agent that used trial history directly. In mice, the state-dependent RPE and its trace added little predictive information beyond observable trial history, which limits what choice prediction alone can reveal about prediction-error learning.

papers.title: Functional cell type diversity in the Drosophila lamina is established by a single transcription factor dFezf, controlling a large repertoire of ion channels and receptors
papers.abstract: Neuronal cell types in the brain can show remarkable diversity in their functional properties. In the visual system, neurons at different levels of hierarchy show diverse kinetics, leading to the encoding of different features of the visual scene. How this behaviorally relevant diversification is achieved is not understood. Here, we address this question in a simple system, studying two visual cell types in Drosophila that diversify their responses despite receiving the same photoreceptor input to encode two distinct basic visual features, contrast and luminance. We first show that this cell type diversity is mostly established by cell-intrinsic mechanism. While cell-type specific transcriptome analysis delivers promising receptor and channel candidates, genetic manipulation of these differentially regulated genes fails to identify individual channels or receptors that are necessary or sufficient for the functional differences between luminance-sensitive L3 neurons and contrast-sensitive L2 neurons. However, loss of the L3-specific transcription factor dFezf makes L3 neurons transient and contrast-sensitive. Interestingly, dFezf controls the cell-type-specific expression of several receptors and ion channels that we initially found to be differentially expressed between L2 and L3. Together, this argues for a degenerate system in which multiple genes jointly shape cell type-specific functional properties. Our finding that a single transcription factor regulates the expression of such a set of genes that can be relevant for function suggest that similar regulation might also be in place in other degenerate systems, which exist widely across cell types, brain regions, and species.

papers.title: Social environment induces reversible remodeling of the adult primate brain
papers.abstract: Patterns of social contact can change abruptly, but whether their effects on brain architecture persist or recede when original conditions return remains unclear. Here we followed 13 adult male macaques through three successive phases of single housing, protected-contact paired housing, and restored single housing, acquiring structural and functional MRI and measuring hair cortisol at approximately three-month intervals, with two assessments per phase. Paired housing was associated with grey-matter expansion across temporal association cortex and several subcortical and brainstem structures. Concurrently, default-mode- and limbic-associated regions shifted within a functional-connectivity manifold, while hair cortisol increased. When single housing was restored, grey-matter and cortisol elevations receded, and regional functional changes reversed direction. These trajectories identify a reversible component of adult primate brain architecture that tracks current social conditions.

papers.title: Network-related variations of cerebrovascular status are correlated with cognitive control performance
papers.abstract: Cerebrovascular health has emerged as a crucial factor in influencing cognitive decline in aging, including cognitive control and fluid intelligence. Previous studies have largely relied on peripheral assessments of vascular health due to the paucity of global and regional estimates of cerebrovascular status. This study uses the pulse relaxation function (PReFx), a measure of pulse-wave shape based on diffuse optical tomography (pulse-DOT), to provide regional estimates of arterial elasticity in the cortical mantle. For the first time, we integrate a network-based approach based on previous fMRI studies and pulse-DOT regional mapping of cerebrovascular status, to test whether the support provided by the cerebrovascular system to different brain networks may differentially impact cognitive control performance. To comprehensively assess how various mechanisms of cognitive control are influenced by the cerebrovascular health of different networks, we used a task-switching paradigm that simultaneously measures proactive and reactive control processes. After removing the global signal, we found that larger positive PReFx residual values in the Dorsal Attention and Visual Networks are linked to lower cognitive control costs. Conversely, larger positive residual values in the Default Mode and Fronto-Parietal Networks are associated with higher cognitive control costs. These results indicate that the relative balance of arterial elasticity across different brain networks impacts cognitive control, highlighting the importance of studying network-based cerebrovascular status for understanding cognitive performance.

papers.title: Lightness illusions and saliency maps for reflectance estimation are similar across a wide range of deep neural network architectures
papers.abstract: People perform many visual tasks that depend on having representations that remain correlated with surface reflectance despite large variations in illumination and context. This ability is known as `lightness constancy'. Developing image-computable models of lightness constancy has been challenging, but we recently showed that deep neural networks trained for reflectance estimation achieve good performance on some lightness tasks, and furthermore are susceptible to many of the same lightness illusions as human observers. Here we extend this work by testing whether these findings are specific to the network architecture we used in our previous work, or whether they generalize broadly across architectures and training procedures. We evaluated a range of architectures (ResUNet, VGGUNet, MobileUNet, and Dense Prediction Transformer) that we trained to estimate reflectance from rendered images of three-dimensional scenes. We compared networks where the initial, stimulus-encoding phase used pre-trained weights learned for other tasks, and networks where all weights were optimized for reflectance estimation. We found that all architectures and training procedures tested produced similar reflectance estimation performance on held-out images, and were susceptible to several classic lightness illusions. Furthermore, saliency analyses showed that all networks had broadly similar spatial sensitivity across input images. Together, these results suggest that lightness constancy and susceptibility to lightness illusions do not depend strongly on details of network architecture and training, but instead often emerge robustly in networks that have been optimized to infer surface reflectance from luminance.

papers.title: How reliable is the link between effort and nucleus accumbens connectivity at rest? A psychometric evaluation of repeated assessments
papers.abstract: Individuals differ in their willingness to work for rewards. Although effort-based behavior shows trait-like stability and motivational traits associate with functional connectivity (FC), it remains unclear how robustly individual differences in effort are reflected in intrinsic FC of reward circuits. Here, we investigated whether effort-based behavior and questionnaire scores are reflected in nucleus accumbens (NAcc) FC. To this end, we evaluated this association in 84 healthy adults (43 women, 41 men), who completed five sessions of an effort allocation task and two task-free fMRI scans, each collected on different days to capture trait-like behavior and brain function. First, behavioral measures showed high test-retest reliability across sessions (ICCs: 0.62-0.83). Second, NAcc FC showed the highest reliability in subcortical regions (ICCs = 0.59-0.69), while cortical connections were heterogeneous and, overall, less reliable. Higher effort exertion was associated with stronger NAcc IFG FC (tmax(76) = 4.65, pFWE = .041, k = 141), while greater sensitivity to task difficulty was associated with stronger NAcc subcallosal gyrus FC (tmax(76) = -5.15, pFWE = .028, k = 155). Intriguingly, the association of effort exertion with NAcc IFG FC decreased over behavioral sessions, whereas the association of sensitivity to cost (difficulty) with NAcc subcallosal FC was stable over behavioral sessions. Our findings show that identifying robust brain-behavior associations likely requires comparable multi-session approaches, at least in moderately sized samples. Beyond reliability, such approaches may also help reveal additional insights about the temporal profile of brain-behavior associations, which may differ markedly for new versus routine task performance.

papers.title: 5-HT2A receptor deletion is associated with reduced hippocampal parvalbumin levels and anxiety-like behavior in BALB/c mice
papers.abstract: The serotonin 2A receptor (5-HT2AR) is a target of drugs used to treat anxiety and mood disorders, yet whether endogenous 5-HT2AR signaling constrains or promotes anxiety, and how the 5-HT2AR affects cell populations linked to anxiety, is not fully resolved. Acute 5-HT2AR agonism is anxiolytic and acts through the activation of ventral hippocampal parvalbumin-expressing interneurons. Here we report that constitutive deletion of the 5-HT2AR in male and female BALB/c mice is associated with robust anxiety-like and repetitive behavior across multiple paradigms. Unbiased proteomic analysis of male knockout hippocampal tissue revealed substantially reduced levels of parvalbumin (PV), a proxy of their activity. Consistent with the intense metabolic demands of fast spiking interneurons, proteins supporting energy metabolism were also downregulated, including those related to oxidative phosphorylation and the electron transport chain, glycolysis and the tricarboxylic acid cycle, together with the cytoplasmic ribosome. In terms of how reduced 5-HT2AR signaling could lead to reduced PV expression, we examined key perineuronal net (PNN) components. The PNN constituents aggrecan and HAPLN1 were not significantly changed, whereas the link protein, HAPLN4 was substantially reduced. In a separate cohort, 7 days following a single dose of the selective 5-HT2AR agonist, 25CN-NBOH, many of the same energy metabolism proteins were shifted in the opposite direction. Together these findings indicate that constitutive loss of 5-HT2AR signaling is associated with coordinated reductions in parvalbumin and in the biosynthetic and bioenergetic machinery that supports fast-spiking activity, without a generalized loss of perineuronal net structural components.

papers.title: TSPAN10 Loss-of-Function in hESC-Derived RPE Reveals Critical Roles in Pigmentation, Polarity, and Antioxidant Defence
papers.abstract: Expression quantitative trait loci studies have highlighted TSPAN10 as a gene that confers an increased risk of developing age-related macular degeneration (AMD). The mechanism for this and the role of TSPAN10 in retinal cells such as the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and its contribution to AMD pathology are unknown. We report the generation of human embryonic stem cell derived RPE with TSPAN10 knockout using CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing. This provided an in vitro model to investigate the functions of TSPAN10. TSPAN10 knockout cells were differentiated into mature RPE. Significant differences were observed in cell pigmentation, polarisation and cell body height, and the response to oxidative stress in comparison to wild type. These results demonstrate for the first time a role for TSPAN10 in the RPE, aligning with published data to support the importance of TSPAN10 for pigmentation, and adding to our understanding of the heterogeneous disease AMD.

papers.title: Distinct roles of microglial and neuronal P2X4 in persistent neuropathic pain
papers.abstract: Neuropathic pain is a chronic, debilitating condition characterized by persistent sensory hypersensitivity and frequently associated with anxiety- and depression. Although microglial P2X4 receptors are well-established mediators of early neuropathic pain, their cell-specific contributions to pain maintenance and associated affective disturbances remains poorly understood. We investigated these contributions in male and female mice 30 and 60 days after spared nerve injury (SNI) using conditional P2X4 deletion in microglia (Cx3cr1CreERT2) or neurons (Synapsin-1-Cre), behavioral assessments, and in vivo recordings of spinal dorsal horn wide dynamic range neurons. Microglial P2X4 deletion before SNI completely prevented mechanical allodynia whereas deletion initiated 40 days after injury fully reversed established allodynia in both sexes. Notably, P2X4 immunoreactivity was undetectable in spinal microglia at the late time points examined, suggesting that the sustained contribution of microglial P2X4 may involve mechanisms outside the spinal microglial compartment. Neuronal P2X4 deletion partially attenuated mechanical hypersensitivity and reduced dorsal horn neurons hyperexcitability at day 60 after SNI, supporting a modulatory role in persistent spinal sensitization. Global P2X4 deletion prevented anxiety- and depressive-like behaviors that emerged by day 30 in males and day 60 in females. Whether this protection reflects a direct contribution of P2X4 to affective disturbances or an indirect consequence of reduced pain remains unresolved. Together, these findings identify distinct microglial and neuronal P2X4 contributions to established neuropathic pain and reveal sex-dependent differences in the onset of associated affective disturbances.

papers.title: Motor learning engages intrinsic plasticity in the human cortex
papers.abstract: Learning is commonly explained by changes in synaptic strength. In animals, however, learning also engages intrinsic plasticity -- changes in how readily neurons convert synaptic input into firing. Its contribution to human learning has been unclear, because conventional non-invasive measures of cortical excitability primarily reflect synaptic strength. Here we used controllable-pulse transcranial magnetic stimulation to estimate two biophysical indices of intrinsic excitability in human motor cortex, before and after motor training. Training produced signatures of increased intrinsic excitability, selectively in the cortical representation of the trained muscle, but not an untrained muscle. Individuals showing larger intrinsic excitability changes learned faster, independently of changes in motor-evoked potential amplitude, an index of synaptic excitability that increased following training but did not predict learning rate. An axon model reproduced the measured changes through small shifts in membrane excitability. These findings provide evidence that intrinsic plasticity is expressed in the intact human brain, and that it represents a behaviourally relevant component of learning-related cortical adaptation.

papers.title: A CT-to-brain-atlas mapping framework using cranial base landmarks in marmosets
papers.abstract: Objective. The common marmoset (Callithrix jacchus), a small, experimentally tractable nonhuman primate, is increasingly used as a model for studying higher brain functions. However, substantial individual differences in its skull and brain limit the accuracy of stereotaxic coordinates. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of each animal improves accuracy but is costly. Computed tomography (CT) is easy to acquire and shows the skull and implanted devices, but not the brain. We therefore aimed to map CT images to a brain atlas without MRI of each animal. Approach. Six marmosets with both CT and MR images served as references. A target CT image was registered to a reference CT image and mapped to the atlas via the reference's MR image. For this CT-to-CT registration, we compared intensity-based registration with landmark-based registration using eight cranial base landmarks. We also averaged mappings across multiple references. Mapping error was measured against the mapping via the target's own MR image. Main results. With a single reference, landmark-based registration had a significantly smaller error than intensity-based registration. Averaging the mappings from five references improved the accuracy (0.45 mm), and five or more landmarks gave almost the same accuracy as all eight. Landmark-based registration also worked better on CT images from a different scanner and on postoperative CT images with implants (three and two marmosets, respectively). Using our new open-source software, Marmoset Atlas Mapper, we assigned Neuropixels recording sites to brain regions on postoperative CT, and the region boundaries were qualitatively consistent with boundaries in local field potential correlations. Significance. Cranial base landmarks and multiple references allow CT-to-atlas mapping with a submillimeter mean error without MRI of each animal, even with image artifacts or partly missing landmarks. This enables in vivo localization of implanted devices, including those in deep structures, facilitating studies of higher brain functions in marmosets.

papers.title: MLE EEG Toolbox: A Personal AI Laboratory Assistant for Literature-Informed and Reproducible M/EEG Research
papers.abstract: Electrophysiological research increasingly relies on complex analytical workflows, yet integrating methodological evidence, computational execution and reproducibility remains challenging. Here we introduce MLE EEG Toolbox, a framework for building a personal AI laboratory assistant for electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetoencephalography (MEG) research. The toolbox integrates locally deployed AI, natural-language-guided analysis, literature retrieval and methodological comparison, and reproducible computational workflows. A constrained language model translates research instructions into validated, researcher-approved operations, while literature-informed guidance supports parameter selection and protocol reconstruction. Computational provenance enables transparent inspection and replay of analytical workflows. The assistant achieved action-selection accuracies of 85.6% for EEG and 95.5% for MEG, while 142 cross-platform tests demonstrated close numerical agreement. Applications to public EEG and MEG datasets illustrated integrated spectral, network, decoding and source analyses. Running on standard personal computers without external AI APIs or token charges, MLE EEG Toolbox provides an accessible, researcher-controlled environment that connects methodological knowledge with reproducible electrophysiological analysis.

papers.title: Diet-Induced Obesity is Associated with Sex-Dependent Cerebral Microvascular Changes and Cognitive Decline in Mice
papers.abstract: Metabolic diseases, including obesity and diabetes, are major risk factors for cognitive impairment and dementia, yet the underlying causal mechanisms remain unclear. Here we investigate whether this link is mediated by dysfunctional changes in cerebral microvessels. Using a multimodal longitudinal approach combining 3D light-sheet fluorescence microscopy, contrast-enhanced MRI and cognitive testing, we characterise structural, functional and behavioural changes to the brain microvasculature in a mixed-sex mouse model of diet-induced obesity (DIO). Our results reveal a striking sex-specific vulnerability to obesity-driven cerebrovascular dysfunction. Brains from male DIO mice exhibited reduced capillary diameter and volume in the frontal cortex, alongside decreased blood volume and accelerated cognitive decline over time in an object recognition task. Conversely, female DIO mice displayed compensatory capillary vasodilation and were protected against neurovascular and cognitive impairment. These findings link cerebral microvascular changes to obesity-associated cognitive decline, and identify sex-dependent differences in the cerebrovascular response to obesity.

papers.title: Universal barcoded connectomics for massively parallel single-neuron projection mapping in diverse vertebrate species
papers.abstract: Neuroscience relies on diverse model species to understand animal behavior and brain function. Yet, tools for rapid, high-resolution brain connectivity mapping remain unavailable in most vertebrate species, slowing progress in many neuroscience models and rendering cross-species circuit comparisons challenging. Here, we overcome this barrier by establishing sequencing-based barcoded connectomics for rapid single-neuron tracing in seven vertebrate species ranging from frogs to birds to non-human primates. We develop a general solution to viral tropism and barcode trafficking, validate our reagents by mapping the projections of thousands of neurons in the songbird HVC, and discover a single set of reagents that functions across highly divergent species. Together, we provide ready-to-use barcoding reagents for diverse species and a simple framework for further adapting them if necessary, enabling high throughput single-neuron tracing across vertebrates.

papers.title: Evolutionarily conserved coupling of lysosomal response sensing and disease-associated microglial reprogramming scales with pathological timescales
papers.abstract: Background Microglia transition into disease-associated microglia (DAM) during central nervous system (CNS) injury and neurodegeneration, yet the upstream intracellular logic driving this state conversion in vivo remains unclear. The lysosome acts as a signaling hub, but whether physiological phagocytic load universally initiates and quantitatively couples to DAM reprogramming across different pathological timescales is unknown. Methods We established a rigorous, unit-corrected analytical framework to overcome pseudo-replication in public single-cell data, anchoring statistical inferences at the level of independent biological units (animals, sequencing plates, or donors). We integrated six transcriptomic datasets spanning three murine injury/amyloidosis models and three large-scale human neurodegenerative cohorts (>320,000 microglial nuclei), alongside human Alzheimer's disease (AD) GWAS summary statistics. Results We demonstrate that the MiT/TFE-regulated lysosomal biogenesis program temporally precedes DAM reprogramming and maintains an evolutionarily conserved baseline coupling even in uninjured homeostatic tissue. In human microglia, MITF and TFE3 transcripts closely track DAM activation, whereas post-translationally regulated TFEB mRNA does not. Genetic enrichment analysis (MAGMA) reveals that common AD risk does not act upon the upstream lysosomal program, but is strongly anchored downstream at APOE. Furthermore, Trem2-knockout models demonstrate that disease-induced coupling amplification retains roughly half its magnitude even when the mature DAM subpopulation collapses. Cross-system comparisons reveal a state-transition synchrony model: disease-driven amplification of lysosomal-DAM coupling ({Delta}) scales with pathological timescales, showing strong amplification in acute murine injury and aggressive amyloidosis (5xFAD {Delta} = +0.252), but manifesting primarily as steady baseline maintenance across decades-long asynchronous human AD progression (SEA-AD {Delta} = +0.072). Conclusions Our study establishes the lysosomal stress-DAM coupling as an evolutionarily conserved pacemaking module for microglial state transitions, providing a quantitative framework for therapeutically targeting neuroinflammation and tissue repair.

papers.title: Neonatal exposure to SARS-CoV-2 spike protein in mice is associated with localized changes in cerebral cortex cell proliferation
papers.abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) can cause acute and persistent neurological manifestations, and evidence suggests these effects may be at least partly explained by direct effects of Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) spike protein, which includes neuroinflammation, cognitive dysfunction, and persistent pain. Because the developing brain undergoes finely regulated processes of cellular proliferation, differentiation, and cerebrovascular maturation, exposure to SARS-CoV-2 or its components during this critical period may interfere with neurodevelopment. We therefore investigated whether neonatal exposure to the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein affects processes underlying brain development. To this end, we used a mouse model previously developed by our group, where Swiss mice received an injection (s.c.) of spike protein from the ancestral viral strain or vehicle at postnatal day 1 (P1). Body weight, body length, and the righting reflex were evaluated until postnatal day 20 (P20). At P10, mouse brains were analyzed for cell proliferation, neural cell populations, and cerebrovascular organization, while blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability was assessed at P20 using Evans Blue. Neonatal spike protein exposure did not affect body weight, body length, or postural righting reflex. At P10, cell proliferation in spike-exposed animals was comparable to control groups, whereas region-specific alterations in SOX2-positive cells and TBR1-positive neurons were observed. Spike protein exposure did not broadly alter cerebrovascular architecture or BBB permeability, although increased IB4 fluorescence was detected in the lateral dentate gyrus (DG). Our findings provide evidence that exposure to the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein during postnatal development can influence specific aspects of neural development, highlighting the importance of understanding how viral components may affect the developing brain during critical windows of vulnerability. Keywords: spike protein, brain development, coronavirus, COVID-19, SARS-CoV-2, cerebrovasculature.

papers.title: Shox2 maintains thalamocortical neuron firing for whisker-based somatomotor responses and sleep spindles in mice
papers.abstract: In the mouse thalamus, thalamocortical neurons (TCNs) relay sensory information to cortex and generate rhythmic activity, including sleep spindles, through precisely timed firing. TCNs switch between tonic and burst firing modes that depend on intrinsic membrane properties, yet what maintains these properties in the mature thalamus remains unknown. Transcription factors, which regulate the ion channel genes that shape firing, are natural candidates. Here, we investigate Shox2, a transcription factor implicated in rhythmic activity across multiple systems, in ventral posterior medial (VPM) thalamus. Using genetic labeling and optogenetic activation, we show that Shox2 expressing neurons form functional thalamocortical and thalamoreticular projections capable of driving cortical responses. Conditional knockout of Shox2 in VPM alters intrinsic membrane properties, reducing both tonic and burst firing without altering thalamocortical circuit organization or barrel field architecture. These firing deficits are accompanied by impaired whisker-dependent somatomotor performance and a reduction in sleep spindle density in cortical target regions, while overall sleep architecture remains intact. Together, these findings identify Shox2 as a transcriptional regulator required to maintain intrinsic firing modes in VPM thalamocortical neurons, linking a transcription factor to spindle deficits, an emerging neurophysiological biomarker for autism spectrum disorder and schizophrenia.

papers.title: Music and speech dissociate local temporal irregularity from response strength in human superior temporal cortex
papers.abstract: Speech and music engage overlapping auditory cortex. We asked whether they shape the timing of local activity in ways that regional response strength alone leaves unresolved. In intracranial recordings from 30 participants watching a film with alternating music and speech, 1-10-Hz activity in the superior temporal gyrus (STG) had higher sample entropy during music, indicating that similar short patterns were less likely to persist (mean paired difference = 0.02256, FDR q = 0.00753). The contrast persisted in comparisons of adjacent film blocks and was larger relative to surrogate signals matched for amplitude distribution and approximate power spectrum. Speech elicited higher STG high-frequency power in the intracranial subset and stronger bilateral STG BOLD responses in all 30 participants in the separately acquired fMRI recordings. Together, these findings show that the soundtrack category associated with stronger regional responses differs from the one associated with greater local temporal irregularity. The temporal organisation of local activity therefore adds a dimension to how shared auditory cortex responds to natural sounds.

papers.title: Local and network-level dynamics of alpha and beta rhythms during visuospatial attention in autism
papers.abstract: Visuospatial attention is altered in autism, yet the underlying neural mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Neural oscillatory activity coordinates distributed processes supporting attentional selection and their flexible adjustment to changing environmental demands. Altered oscillatory organization may therefore provide a mechanistic basis for atypical attentional processing in autism. We tested this theory using EEG recordings from 80 autistic and neurotypical children and youth performing a spatial cueing task with valid and invalid cues. We quantified alpha- and beta-band measures of local power and inter-trial phase clustering (ITPC) together with power- and phase-based measures of posterior-frontal long-range connectivity. Across validity conditions, autistic participants showed a more frontal alpha distribution, reduced posterior alpha lateralization and posterior beta ITPC, and higher frontal beta power. Crucially, autistic participants also presented reduced neural adaptation across attentional conditions, reflected in attenuated validity-dependent modulation of alpha power and of posterior-frontal beta connectivity, with elevated beta connectivity particularly in the valid cue condition. This neural pattern was accompanied by greater reaction-time slowing in the invalid compared with the valid cue condition. Within autistic participants, beta dynamics showed nominal associations with restricted and repetitive behaviors that did not survive multiple-comparison correction. Together, these findings suggest that visuospatial attention in autism is characterized by altered local oscillatory organization, combined with reduced modulation of local and distributed dynamics as attentional demands change. Alterations in alpha and beta activity may reflect reduced spatially selective attentional gating alongside greater maintenance of established attentional states.

papers.title: Modelling vortex interactions reveals distinct patterns of brain reconfiguration following psilocybin and escitalopram
papers.abstract: Major depressive disorder is a leading cause of disability, yet how interventions reorganise brain dynamics remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated how psilocybin and escitalopram reshape brain dynamics in depression using pre- and post-treatment resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) from a double-blind randomised controlled trial (NCT03429075). We compared two whole-brain modelling approaches: conventional signal-space modelling describing interactions between regional brain signals, and vortex-space modelling capturing interactions between evolving patterns of local synchronisation. This represents the first application of vortex-space modelling to a psychiatric disorder. Vortex space was more sensitive than signal space in most analyses, including distinguishing treatment-related brain states, relating baseline connectivity to clinical improvement and predicting response to escitalopram. Our results further revealed distinct patterns of reorganisation following the two interventions. Psilocybin produced widespread increases in vortex-space effective connectivity and reduced network modularity, whereas escitalopram showed no comparable changes. Despite these differences, greater increases in brain turbulence (i.e., spatiotemporal variability in local synchronisation) were associated with greater symptom reduction in both treatments, with a significant post-treatment increase in responders. These findings suggest that psilocybin and escitalopram may reorganise brain dynamics in markedly different ways and yet share dynamical features associated with clinical improvement. Overall, vortex-space modelling offers a promising framework for characterising brain dynamics in depression and its successful treatment.

papers.title: Data-Driven Decomposition of Precisely Aligned Fiber-Orientation-Preserving Probabilistic Tractography Connectomes with Non-Negative Matrix Factorization
papers.abstract: The major goals of the Human Connectome Project (HCP) were to characterize the structural and functional connectivity of the human brain. Although there has been tremendous work done for functional connectivity, including application of a variety of data driven decomposition approaches, structural connectivity from the HCP has seen less attention. This work presents a collection of methodological advances that, in combination, enable similar approaches to be applied to diffusion tractography data. Here, we use multi-modal non-linear volumetric alignment with FSL's MultiMOdal Registration Framework (MMORF) to precisely align white matter tracts and globular gray matter nuclei, use the White matter Hierarchical Modelling (WHIM) method to align voxel-wise fiber orientations, enable efficient GPU-accelerated computation and storage of full resolution probabilistic gray matter x white matter x fiber sparse tractography matrices in precise alignment across individuals using the aforementioned MMORF and WHIM alignments together with areal-feature-based cortical surface registration. These tractography dense connectomes can be averaged across individuals and sparse, computationally efficient non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) can be applied to perform data-driven decompositions into white matter tracts and gray matter projection territories. The primary outputs of this effort to date are 1) A set of HCP software pipelines enabling such analyses, 2) A new unbiased HCP-derived volumetric standard space that is representative of the young adult brain and follows ACPC orientation conventions across individuals. 3) Reproducible NMF decompositions of HCP young adult tractography data into white matter tracts and gray matter projection territories, which could be projected using non-negative dual regression back to individuals. These data represent a starting point for a new generation of data-driven atlasing efforts for human white matter, and these methods can be applied to study the white matter in development, aging, and brain diseases.

papers.title: ASTEROID, A Validated Annotated Dataset of Analytical Decisions in Graph Theory Based fMRI
papers.abstract: Graph theory-based functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) studies use complex analytical pipelines, but methodological decisions are often reported in unstructured text, limiting systematic comparison and the design of multiverse analyses. Here, we describe ASTEROID, a structured annotation dataset derived from 156 graph theory-based human fMRI study publications. Its schema contains 125 labels, comprising 61 methodological labels and 64 labels for study characteristics and experimental design. An LLM-assisted workflow generated initial annotations, which underwent automated quality-control checks and expert human review. The dataset captures preprocessing, functional connectivity, and graph-analysis decisions. Within these categories, steps and their sequence, software, algorithms, parameters, and supporting text spans are included where available. This accompanying paper provides prompt specifications, processing scripts, and documentation, and describes an interactive viewer that supports exploration of the annotation schema and the study records. ASTEROID enables comparison of reported analytical choices, the informed design of multiverse-based robustness analysis and supports the development and evaluation of automated methodological information-extraction tools and educational resources for fMRI data analysis.
